reader.requirement: At 1985 argument-1 of FUNCTION FACTORIAL must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4: an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer): a non-numeric operand, a numeric item with decimal places, a non-integer literal, a numeric (not integer) function and a not-always-integral expression must be refused; the >= 0 half is a value constraint whose violation leaves the result undefined (§1989:A.1.2.2), so 0 and positive integers must evaluate.

reader.notes: The 'i' kind screens class numeric plus IntegerViolation (non-integral item, literal, numeric function, provably non-integral quotient). A negative argument compiles and yields 0, which the text leaves undefined. Messages cite §2023 clauses at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: fact3.cob at --std 85, with WN PIC 9 VALUE 3 and WM PIC 9 VALUE 5. COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL (WN * 0.5), FUNCTION FACTORIAL (0.5 * WN) and FUNCTION FACTORIAL (WN * WM / 2) all compile clean. The program runs and prints 'WN*0.5 1', '0.5*WN 1' and 'WN*WM/2 5040'. Each argument (1.5, 1.5, 7.5) was silently truncated to an integer. The same compiler refuses FACTORIAL (WN / 2) (the reader's factbad), FACTORIAL (WN + 0.5) and FACTORIAL (WN ** 0.5) (fact1.cob, COBOL1627). So it enforces the 'always integral' requirement for a root quotient, an additive constant and a power, but fails open on a product with a non-integral literal and on a quotient below the root. At --std 2023 it does the same (fact3-002). fact2.cob confirms the accepted half is right: WP PIC 9PP / 25 gave 24, 2.0 gave 2, a signed integer item gave 24, 0.5 * 4 gave 2, FACTORIAL (INTEGER-PART (5.5)) gave 120 and WN ** 2 gave 362880. cite: OK  §1989:A.2.14.3 AR1  (2.14.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR1. OK  §1989:A.2.2 AR4  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in AR4 ('An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified'). OK  §1989:A.1.2.2. The design (docs/INTRINSICS_DESIGN.md, PB1526) makes the screen fail-open on purpose and relies on run-time EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. The 1989 module has no exception condition for that check to raise, and at --std 85 the truncation is silent. The project ruled the sibling shape (N ** 0.5 at --std 85, 1989-AR-A.2.2-4) OVERTURNED as under-rejects and fixed it in kb/Work PB5208. Its landing added only a power arm; the product shape is not in the design's recorded list of fail-open shapes.
refuter.corrected: Non-conforming, harm under-rejects, cause b (same at --std 2023). Repro: 01 WN PIC 9 VALUE 3. ... COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL (WN * 0.5). Expected: refused, because the argument does not always result in an integer value (§1989:A.2.2 AR4); the same compiler refuses WN / 2 at this position. Observed: it compiles and prints 1 (FACTORIAL of 1.5 truncated to 1). The mechanism is IntrinsicArgumentRules.NotAlwaysIntegral: it has no product witness arm (an item times a non-integral literal whose granularity the literal does not cancel), and its quotient arm fires only at the root. Known notes: PB5208 (landed; the power sibling) and PB1526 (landed; the 2023 run-time half). No open note covers the product shape.
